audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed on all seven rows, AND the content prose claimed Fizz has a range advantage over Pantheon — which is backwards.
audit.why: Full phases[].side read [Pantheon x4, Skill x3]; content win[0..6] read Fizz on all seven. The page's own difficulty verdict is TRICKY 7/10 with Pantheon carry threat 7.5/10, which matches the Pantheon-early reading, not the all-Fizz reading. The kit settles it: Comet Spear is a 575-range spear throw, Shield Vault is a 600-range point-and-click dash-stun on 13/12/11/10/9s, and Fizz is melee with a 550 Q. A melee assassin does not out-range that. Fizz's pole arrives at 3 and the shark at 6, which is when the lane turns.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 set to Pantheon on BOTH layers with all four whys rewritten to describe him winning; rows 4-6 set to Fizz on both layers. Ratings on rows 0-3 dropped from 7/10 to 3/10 so the number stops contradicting the side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grand Starfall was called a lane-irrelevant roam tool with no cooldown given, and Aegis Assault's duration/cooldown never appeared.
audit.why: Grand Starfall is 180/165/150s at 5500 range — a genuine map-wide spike, and its 180s rank-1 cooldown is what makes punishing his absence worth doing. Aegis Assault is 22/21/20/19/18s and blocks frontal damage while he channels, which is the reason a staggered string beats a dumped one.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[1].text and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield Vault's auto-attack reset — the actual burst tell — was never mentioned, and Aegis Assault was described as a 'parry' that only works 'on read'.
audit.why: Shield Vault carries the autoReset flag: his combo opens with an attack reset, so the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the cast (this is the missingInteractions entry for this matchup). Aegis Assault is a channel that makes him invulnerable to damage from the FRONT while striking repeatedly — it is not a read-dependent parry, it is a directional block on a 22s cooldown, and it is channel-flagged, so hard CC cancels it. Chum the Waters' knockup is the CC Fizz has for that.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and the content early paragraph.

audit.why: Shield Vault 13/12/11/10/9s, Aegis Assault 22/21/20/19/18s, Grand Starfall 180/165/150s are all in the kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names used throughout the content layer: 'Aegis Protection' and 'Grand Skyfall'.
audit.why: Pantheon's abilities are Mortal Will, Comet Spear, Shield Vault, Aegis Assault, Grand Starfall. 'Aegis Protection' appears in whys[2], spikes[2].text, the early paragraph and wants.foe[0]; 'Grand Skyfall' appears in spikes[1].text, the mid paragraph and wants.foe[2] (the packet flagged the last one).
audit.corrected: Every occurrence corrected to the real name.

notes:
THIS WAS THE WORST MATCHUP IN MY SLICE. The content layer was written as if Fizz out-ranges Pantheon — 'he has no ranged tool to threaten you from a distance', 'play around your longer effective range', 'deny his short-range all-ins with your range advantage', 'poke him down with Chum the Waters'. Fizz is melee (Q is 550); Comet Spear is a 575-range throw and Shield Vault is a 600-range point-and-click dash-stun. That advice loses games, and it was repeated across early, mid, late, whys[0], wants.you[1] and spikes[3]. All of it is rewritten.

CHART — please review this one. The two layers disagreed on all seven rows: full read [Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Skill, Skill, Skill] and content read Fizz on all seven, and the packet levelChart also reads Fizz on all seven. I resolved it TOWARD the full layer for rows 0-3 rather than toward the packet, because the kit is unambiguous that a melee assassin does not win levels 1-3 against a 575-range spear plus a 600-range point-and-click stun, and because the page's own verdict is TRICKY 7/10 with Pantheon carry threat 7.5/10 — an all-Fizz chart cannot coexist with that rating. Rows 4-6 go to Fizz on both layers. This is the only place in my slice where I moved a row AGAINST the packet, so it is the one to check.

TWO FABRICATED ABILITY NAMES: 'Aegis Protection' (real name Aegis Assault) in four fields, and 'Grand Skyfall' (real name Grand Starfall) in three. The packet only caught one of the seven.

UNVERIFIED, not written: whether Chum the Waters' knockup actually cancels the Aegis Assault channel (the kit flags the ability as channel/'interruptible — any CC cancels it', but I could not confirm a knockup specifically interrupts it), and whether Playful/Trickster's untargetability dodges the Shield Vault dash-stun outright or only its damage. I wrote 'knocks him out of Aegis Assault' in dosFull[2].d on the strength of the channel flag — if that flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire, that one line should be reverted.
